fun_highlights: The 2-3 minute burst format is genuinely well-served by the pacing: you tap in, years pass in ambient text, then a card lands with a real question. The moment of pause before choosing is satisfying on a small screen.

Callback cards are a genuine delight when they fire — seeing 'A kindness done at 6 came back, decades later, as a door held open' closes a loop that landed in a previous session. That's the best hit the game delivers.
Early childhood cards (stray animal, the book too hard, the sibling arriving) have a specific warmth that makes the opening minutes of each life feel fresh and human.
Dying a founder at 7 or 8 (as in Dynasties 3, 4, 9) and immediately starting over is a sharp, honest jolt — it underlines the dynastic stakes without any ceremony.
The bequest choice (knowledge / coins / warmth / freedom) is the single best cross-session lever: it's a tiny decision with real downstream texture.
staleness: By dynasty 4 or 5, the love-marriage-child spine has become fully predictable. Almost every life in the transcripts hits: meet someone in youth → marry late (40s-50s) → have one child late → child inherits. The engine strongly enforces this template even with player refusals. The 'one more life' pull fades when you know the skeleton in advance.

Several cards appear in almost every single life regardless of dynasty: c_sick (fever), y_mentor (show up every day), a_marry, a_child, x_honest_or_kind, a_conviction/keep it private. After 5-6 lives on a mobile device you are reading the same prose beats with different proper nouns.

The 'honest or kind' dilemma (x_honest_or_kind) fired in dynasty 1 life 1 at 67, dynasty 2 life 1 at 27 AND 52, dynasty 2 life 2 at 42, dynasty 5 life 1 at 35, dynasty 6 life 1 at 55, and many more. It has no cooldown long enough. By dynasty 3 you have memorized both options and the outcome text.

In a 2-3 minute snack session you often get 0-1 choices and mostly observe ambient lines, which are also recycled ('The stairs have started to ask a question of him', 'She still laughs like someone the years have not yet learned how to reach'). On a short burst this can mean nothing to interact with at all.

The dynasty-layer levers (seat investment, reputation gates, reckoning) rarely fire in a typical life — in 38 lives across 12 dynasties they appear sparsely. From a mobile snacker's view the dynasty feels passive, not steerable. Most sessions feel like witnessing rather than building.
Death-at-8 dynasties (3, 4, 9) give no satisfying hit — you get 2-3 cards and it's over. From a mobile angle this registers as wasted session time, not poignant fragility.

improvements.what: Add a hard floor cooldown of 20+ years to x_honest_or_kind and the other 'universal' competing-goods cards (x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty). Or make them once-per-dynasty rather than once-per-life.
improvements.why: These are the cards that most visibly repeat across every life. Seeing the same dilemma prose with a different character name is the defining staleness signal after 4-5 sessions.

improvements.what: Surface one dynasty-layer metric visually at session start — e.g. 'House Fenn: seat 3, scholarly reputation' as a one-line header before the life begins. No numbers elsewhere needed.
improvements.why: Mobile snackers returning after a day have no ambient context for what they're building. A single line of dynasty state would give each burst a goal ('I want to get to seat 4 this life') that transforms witnessing into steering.

improvements.what: Raise the weight of the full-family-differentiation cards (c_sibling, c_animal, c_grandparent, y_dare, y_betray, a_affair) and lower the weight of the skeletal repeat cards (a_marry, a_child when they're forced anyway by the engine) so that the non-spine moments fill more of each short session.
improvements.why: When a 2-minute session gives you only the fever card and a love card, you've played this session before. The rarer characterful moments are what make each life feel like a person — they need higher draw probability.

improvements.what: Give child-death dynasties at least 3 guaranteed non-fever cards before age 8. Currently a life that ends at 8 often delivers 1-2 choices total (fever + maybe one more). On mobile this is a dead session.
improvements.why: The fragility is dramatically interesting conceptually but experientially it means a returned player just burned their 3-minute slot on a life that never opened. Even one more card (the stray dog, the grandparent) would give the brief life texture.

improvements.what: Add a 'this time' variant pool to the 4-5 highest-repetition card texts (y_mentor, a_marry, x_honest_or_kind) — not new logic, just 3-4 additional text framings that the rotI system can cycle through across dynasties rather than lives.
improvements.why: The rotI system rotates per-life but the repeat cadence on mobile (multiple lives per session) means you hit the same text twice in one sitting. A dynasty-level rotation index would break the pattern.

verdict: Each burst has a real quiet hit when a callback fires or a late-life card lands with unexpected weight, but by dynasty 4-5 the love-marry-child skeleton and the recycled 'honest or kind' dilemma have already made the template visible, and a 2-minute snack session is as likely to give you the same four familiar cards as something new.
